title: Align SSE byte-boundaries and function-call ordinality
author: Aisha Raman
description: Motivation: intermittent production errors where SSE-encoded streaming responses occasionally produced partial/unterminated JSON objects or emitted function-call events out of order. Root causes: (1) the reassembly layer operated on token boundaries derived from decoded UTF-8 codepoints, which could shift when fragments split multi-byte sequences; (2) the event queue lacked a stable per-event ordinal when fragments were requeued across windows, allowing a race between tool-call sentinel emission and continuation tokens. This PR aligns reassembly on raw byte anchors and introduces a monotonic per-event ordinal stamped at the producer to guarantee deterministic ordering across reassembly/requeue operations. Changes: - Introduce byte-boundary anchors in sse reassembly to avoid UTF-8 dependent reslicing. - Add event_ordinal metadata propagated with fragments and used to sequence emission in the streamer. - Fast-path: when a function-call sentinel arrives fully contained in a single fragment, emit without requeue to reduce latency. - Normalizes trailing delimiters: collapse repeated trailing delimiters into a single terminal marker to avoid duplicate empty events. - Add deterministic unit and integration tests that reproduce mid-fragment truncation and reorder scenarios. Backwards compatibility: ordinal is internal and does not change wire format for clients; OpenAI-compat adapter preserves existing SSE semantics while guaranteeing ordering. Related: ENG-1079. Checklist: implement reassembly anchors, add ordinals, add tests, CI green, update docs, add changelog entry. Impact: fixes partial JSON failures and rare fn-call ordering regressions observed in canary clusters.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: The new byte_anchor looks good, but I worry about the memory cost of keeping raw offsets for large in-flight windows. Can we cap retention and fall back to conservative resync?
Aisha Raman: Good point — added a sliding retention window with a configurable limit (default 1MB) and fallback resync which preserves correctness at the cost of a one-fragment rollback.
Marta Kowalski: Please add a unit test for zero-length fragment and for repeated delimiter runs — previously we saw duplicate empty events.
Aisha Raman: Added tests for zero-length fragments and delimiter-collapse — included in test_fragment_ordering.py.
Ethan Wu: Minor: prefer relative timestamps for ordinals in logs; otherwise LGTM once CI is green.
Aisha Raman: Switched logs to use relative event_ordinal and added comment explaining why ordinals are monotonic across requeues.

merge_summary: Squash-merged into main after addressing retention cap feedback and adding deterministic tests; CI green on re-run. No migration needed.
release_notes: Fix: SSE streaming stability — prevents partial JSON emission caused by mid-fragment UTF-8 reslicing and ensures function-call events are emitted in producer order. Reduces rare tool-call ordering regressions; no API changes for clients.
testing_notes: Added deterministic reproducer under tests/sse/test_fragment_ordering.py. Reproducer simulates split multi-byte UTF-8 boundaries, repeated delimiters, and cross-window requeueing. Local validation: ran full SSE integration suite against canary cluster (n=3) and simulated 50k fragmented events with zero failures. Bench: fast-path reduced median fncall latency by ~12% in single-fragment cases.
